humanist.name: Luis - Relaxed, Calm and Polished
humanist.rule: the lowest score, then the brief's points, then timbre
humanist.why: Picked by measurement (cast.md §3.3), round 2 at speed 0.80 (Ep1 §AA2). Score 0 with his round-2 takes: 112.6 Hz in the 110-135 Hz lane, 3.0 st under Tasya (Tyler Kurk, 134 Hz) with a timbre distance of 40; at 0.80 he reads 185 wpm, 0.89 of the plan (at 1.0 all four ran 0.61-0.71). The library's 'some breathiness' was checked: CPP 18.2 dB, inside the field's 16.9-20.8 (no breathier than the others). p(en) 0.990 (neutral American); verbatim once 'alright' is read as 'all right'. Bill is next (1.77: still fast at 0.80, a noisier floor). Kyle was screened out (described by ethnicity) and replaced by Grey, who measured fast and noisy (5.70).

engineer.name: Ryan - Articulate, Friendly and Youthful
engineer.rule: the lowest score, then the brief's points, then timbre
engineer.why: Picked by measurement (cast.md §3.4). The only clean read of the off-mic line: the recogniser heard the other three as 'the guy in his computer'. 133.5 Hz, inside the 125-160 Hz lane, 1.9 st under Gerg in the wings (timbre 38.5), 3.2 st under Rima, 11.4 st under CHATGTP; 202 wpm at 1.0 (0.90 of the plan); p(en) 0.999; a light floor penalty (40 dB). For the takes pass: his off-mic line read higher (151 Hz) than his stage line (118 Hz), against the brief's 'lower and closer'; a calmer per-line read for e2-a2-0037/0038 (line_settings) is the fix if the ear agrees. His laugh is a separate take, not auditioned here.

bukaj.name: Scypher
bukaj.rule: the lowest score, then the brief's points, then timbre
bukaj.why: Picked by measurement (cast.md §3.8), round 2 at speed 0.85. The lowest score (0.93): 109.5 Hz (0.1 st under the 110-135 Hz lane), 165 wpm at 0.85 (0.91 of the plan), verbatim, p(en) 0.995, the cleanest floor of the four (60 dB), a narrow 7.8 st range (soft, exact). He sits only 0.7 st under Mas in pitch, but his timbre is 45.9 from Mas's, 4.8x Mas's own spread (9.6). For the ear: if the two-shot blurs, Kenneth (3.2 st under Mas, cached at 0.80) is next. Antoine was out on noise (his floor 13 dB under his speech, a clipped tail).

ekiel.name: Dexter – Customer Support Pro
ekiel.rule: the lowest score, then the brief's points, then timbre
ekiel.why: Picked by measurement (cast.md §3.9), round 2 at speed 0.80. The lowest score (2.43): 110.4 Hz in the 110-140 Hz lane, 1.4 st under MARIO's Kokoro takes (120 Hz) with a timbre distance of 62 (12x Mario's own spread), 3.7 st over Alyi (89 Hz); verbatim; p(en) 0.996; an 8.9 st range (dry, not swinging). His floor is the one weakness (36 dB). At 0.80 'Nobody knows how to do this yet.' still ran quick (1.52 s against the plan's 2.73) and 'You annotated my resignation?' slow (1.95 s against 1.6): the lock fits them, or one retake of e2-a3-0014 if the ear wants it quieter. Brandon (the 'subtle sarcasm' check) had the noisiest floor (23 dB) and wide swings; Mike sits under the lane with a noisier floor.

layered.name: Larry - High-Energy Social Media Voice for Reels & Shorts

crowd.rule: every voice that reads the chant clean (ASR recall >= 0.9 with spelled letters joined, no clipped tail) and p(en) >= 0.95: Ep1's 0.985 bar was set on sentences, and on two seconds of a spelled acronym all twelve read 0.966-0.990, so for the chant it is a gate at 0.95 and otherwise reported; 8-12 layered
crowd.why: Ten of the twelve read the chant cleanly as letters (A.G.I.), with no clipped tail and p(en) of at least 0.95. Eleila read 'A-G-E' and Gutentag's tail was cut. The ten span 104-383 Hz, men and women, each on its own seed (seed_of(line, voice)); layered at 40-180 ms offsets under Alyi's lead.
